title: Custom React.memo Simulator
problemStatement: Implement `memoComponent(Component, arePropsEqual = shallowEqual)` that returns a wrapper function tracking the last rendered props and result. If incoming props are equal to previous props, return the cached result without executing `Component`.
interviewTrap: Not allowing a custom `arePropsEqual` comparator. React allows developers to provide custom comparison functions for complex objects.

testCases.name: Re-uses cached render when props are unchanged
testCases.input: render twice with identical props runs component once
testCases.testFn: let renders = 0; const Comp = (props) => { renders++; return props.name; }; const Memo = memoComponent(Comp, shallowEqual); Memo({ name: 'Alpha' }); Memo({ name: 'Alpha' }); return renders;

testCases.name: Re-renders when props change
testCases.testFn: let renders = 0; const Comp = (props) => { renders++; return props.name; }; const Memo = memoComponent(Comp, shallowEqual); Memo({ name: 'Alpha' }); Memo({ name: 'Beta' }); return renders;

testCases.name: Respects custom comparison function
testCases.testFn: let renders = 0; const Comp = (p) => { renders++; return p.id; }; const Memo = memoComponent(Comp, (a, b) => a.id === b.id); Memo({ id: 1, title: 'Old' }); Memo({ id: 1, title: 'New' }); return renders;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: By default, when a parent component renders, all its child components re-render recursively regardless of whether their props changed. `React.memo` bails out only if all props are shallowly equal.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Component Memoization & Skip Render Decision.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Component Memoization & Skip Render Decision is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Not allowing a custom `arePropsEqual` comparator. React allows developers to provide custom comparison functions for complex objects.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: When should you NOT use React.memo?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: 1) Components that render cheaply (the overhead of shallowEqual can exceed render cost). 2) Components that almost always receive different props (memoization check runs and fails 100% of the time, wasting CPU). 3) Components accepting un-memoized object literals or functions as props.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests practical performance profiling discernment vs premature optimization.

realWorldUseCases.description: Wrapping cell components in React.memo so updating row 5 doesn't re-render 500 other visible rows.

howToExplain.opening: React.memo is a higher-order component that skips rendering when incoming props are shallowly equal to previous props, recycling the previous Fiber.
keyPoints: Wraps component and intercepts render dispatch.
Uses shallowEqual by default; accepts custom comparator.
Only checks props; internal state changes (useState) still trigger re-renders.
Must be paired with useMemo and useCallback on parent props to be effective.
howToExplain.closingImpression: React.memo is a surgical tool for expensive components, not a blanket wrapper for every component.
analogies: A cache of printed documents: if the content didn't change, hand out another copy instead of running the printing press again.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming React.memo prevents re-renders when internal state updates.
commonMistakes.why: React.memo ONLY checks props. If the component's own useState or useContext updates, it re-renders unconditionally.
commonMistakes.correct: Clarify that memoization only skips renders caused by parent updates.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does the upcoming React Compiler (React Forget) change the need for React.memo?
followUpDeepDive.answer: The React Compiler automatically injects fine-grained memoization at the Babel/build step, memoizing values and component JSX blocks automatically, largely eliminating manual `React.memo`, `useMemo`, and `useCallback`.
followUpDeepDive.specReference: React Labs: The React Compiler Architecture
